subsystems.name: Acoustic output driver
subsystems.role: converts amplified electrical signal into sound inside the ear canal; must deliver large gain without distortion in a device the size of an earbud.

subsystems.name: Seal and coupling
subsystems.role: how the bud sits in the ear canal determines bass response and how much sound leaks out and feeds back.
parts: silicone or foam ear tips in several sizes

subsystems.name: Self-fit test
subsystems.role: replaces the clinic booth with a phone-based tone test, estimating hearing thresholds per frequency.
parts: phone or bud playback of test tones

subsystems.name: DSP and fitting engine
subsystems.role: turns the audiogram into a gain curve per frequency band and keeps speech intelligible in noise.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: runs all-day hearing processing, which costs more energy than music playback.

subsystems.name: App and connectivity
subsystems.role: lets the wearer re-test, adjust, and stream audio or calls.

buildSteps.title: Design the acoustics
buildSteps.detail: Engineers model the ear canal and the bud's sealing and venting so the driver's output curve is predictable across ear sizes before any electronics are chosen.

buildSteps.title: Make the drivers
buildSteps.detail: Micro-receivers are wound and assembled under magnification, then tested for output and distortion at full gain.

buildSteps.title: Build the electronics
buildSteps.detail: A low-power audio DSP chip is programmed with the compressor, feedback canceller and beamformer, and combined with microphones and radio on a small rigid-flex board.

buildSteps.title: Write the fitting algorithm
buildSteps.detail: An audiogram-to-gain rule (based on established prescriptions such as NAL-NL2 or DSL, adapted for a sealed earbud) is coded, with limits so output never becomes uncomfortably loud.

buildSteps.title: Develop the self-test
buildSteps.detail: A tone test is validated against clinic audiometry, accounting for the fact that the bud itself plays the test tone, so no external calibration is needed.

buildSteps.title: Close the feedback loop
buildSteps.detail: Acoustic leakage paths are measured and the canceller tuned so the device can supply high gain without squealing — the hardest engineering problem in a self-fit bud.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and test
buildSteps.detail: Units are built and measured on a head-and-torso simulator with a coupler, checking frequency response, gain, distortion and maximum output against the applicable standard.

buildSteps.title: Clear and ship
buildSteps.detail: Devices are validated in studies and sold over the counter, with the wearer running the test and tuning themselves.

prerequisites.why: squeezing clinic-grade gain into a bud depends on small, efficient drivers.
hearing processing, noise reduction and feedback cancellation must run for a full day on a tiny battery.
an on-phone test must be accurate enough that a self-made audiogram is usable.
machine-learning enhancement helps, but the noisy-restaurant case is still the limit of what earbuds achieve.
a self-fitting category is what allows direct sale without a clinic visit.

pathway.milestone: direct-to-consumer self-fitting aids for mild-to-moderate loss
pathway.unlocks: cheaper access for people who never go to a clinic.

pathway.milestone: mainstream consumer earbuds gaining regulated hearing-aid modes
pathway.unlocks: hearing help built into devices people already own and wear.

pathway.milestone: on-device AI scene analysis that adapts automatically to each room
pathway.unlocks: performance approaching clinic-fitted devices without a fitting appointment.

pathway.milestone: self-fitting extended to greater degrees of loss, linked to remote audiology support
pathway.unlocks: most hearing loss managed without a physical clinic visit.
